title: When Voice Matters: Evidence of Gender Disparity in Positional Bias of SpeechLLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating token-level probabilities on multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) benchmarks (including a subset of Spoken StereoSet and a custom occupational ambiguity dataset) to measure the model's selection of stereotypical versus anti-stereotypical options, and analyzing how these selections are asymmetrically influenced by the gender of the input text-to-speech (TTS) voice.

Analyzing the model's token-level probabilities to detect systematic avoidance or preference for specific multiple-choice answer slots (e.g., slot A, B, or C) regardless of the semantic content, and evaluating how this testing artifact interacts with prompt design, inference temperature, and the gender of the input voice.
